title: What Are Gas Fees? Why Sending Crypto Can Cost Extra
caption: Educational only. Not financial advice. Gas fees are network charges paid to process a crypto transaction. They change with demand. Sources: Ethereum.org, Investopedia. AI-generated voice. Educational only. Not financial advice.

scenes.head: WHY THE EXTRA FEE?
scenes.narration: You send crypto and get charged an extra fee. What is it, and why does it keep changing?

scenes.head: WHAT IS GAS?
scenes.narration: Gas is a fee paid to the network for processing your transaction. It usually goes to the computers that keep the network running.

scenes.head: WHY IT CHANGES
scenes.narration: When many people use a network at once, fees can rise. When it is quiet, fees are often lower.

scenes.head: COMPLEX ACTIONS
scenes.narration: Bigger actions, like using smart contracts, usually need more computing work than a simple transfer, so they can cost more.

scenes.head: SMART HABITS
scenes.narration: Check the fee before you confirm, avoid rushing during busy times, and know that different networks charge differently.

scenes.head: REMEMBER
scenes.narration: Fees are usually not refundable, even if a transfer fails, so double check everything. This is education, not advice.
